s1.quote: discovered in 1969 in 7 metres of water on Porpoise Bay near Rottnest Island and Dyer Island

s2.quote: Significant wreckage lies in seven metres (23’) of water with the bow wedged into the reef.

summary.text: A barque wrecked off Rottnest Island in 1878 and now lying in about 7 m, with significant wreckage and the bow jammed into the reef. It is a shallow wreck on the island's heritage trail, protected so nothing may be taken.

s1.quote: Dive down and explore the wrecked Centaur. … The Centaur’s remains lie scattered around the submerged reef, the weed-covered starboard ribs sticking out from its base.

highlights.text: Scattered remains on the reef, weed-covered ribs

s1.quote: 3 – 10 metres … Open Water … 20 – 40+ metres … April to June best … Boat only (Live aboard) … There are still cannons and other artifacts to be seen on the wreck site.

s2.quote: The ship lies in four to six metres of clear Indian Ocean … an excellent dive spot for people of all diving abilities

s3.quote: The wreck remains one of the premier diving sites on the Western Australian coast.

highlights.text: Cannons and anchors still on site

hazards.text: Swell and waves often limit diving

summary.text: The 1629 Dutch East India ship wreck on Morning Reef in the Abrolhos Islands, in only a few metres of clear water. Cannons and other relics remain among coral gardens; it is reached by boat and swell can interrupt diving.

s1.quote: Depths here range from 10 to 15 metres. … large bommies that come close to the surface … The current in this site often brings schools of large and small fish.

highlights.text: Big bommies with rays and leopard sharks

summary.text: Large bommies at the southern end of Julian Rocks off Byron Bay, in roughly 10-15 m. Currents bring schools of fish, and rays and leopard sharks are regular visitors.

s1.quote: At a depth of 12 to 18 metres … sheer walls on either side of the trench … conditions need to be perfect to attempt a swim through.

s2.quote: 15-18m, this is the section to head if you love macro life

hazards.text: Trench swim-through only in perfect conditions

summary.text: A trench between sheer walls at Julian Rocks, about 12-18 m deep, good for macro life and wobbegongs. Swimming through it is only attempted when conditions are right.

s1.quote: varying from 5 to 12 metres … the primary dive site for beginners … frequented by an abundance of reef fish

s2.quote: shallowest part of the are ranging between 5-12m but still packed with fish and turtles!

summary.text: The shallow, sheltered western side of Julian Rocks, about 5-12 m, and the usual choice for beginners. Reef fish are abundant and turtles are often seen.

s1.quote: a series of large bombies, this are is filled with Wobbegongs and Grey Nurse sharks cruising around
opens at a depth of around 15 metres and slopes down to a depth of 21 metres … grey nurse sharks frequent it

s2.quote: this cave is the spot for experienced divers. Ranging from 15-21m it's Grey Nurse shark central!

highlights.text: Grey nurse sharks, moray eels, wobbegongs

summary.text: A swim-through cave at the northern end of Julian Rocks, sloping from about 15 to 21 m. It suits experienced divers and is known for grey nurse sharks.

s1.quote: 12 – 40 metres … Advanced (Supervised open water) … 5 – 30 metres … Wolf Rock is Queensland’s only grey nurse shark gestation site

s2.quote: a set of four volcanic pinnacles two kilometres north-northeast of Double Island Point

summary.text: Volcanic pinnacles off Double Island Point near Rainbow Beach, an advanced dive reaching about 40 m. It is Queensland's key grey nurse shark site, with sharks, eagle rays and seasonal mantas.

s1.quote: Up to 12 metres … 5 – 30 metres … over 100 species of fish
A big field of staghorn coral will lead you to a bommie with healthy coral. … Going with the current you have a chance to see the majestic manta rays

highlights.text: Staghorn coral field and bommie; manta rays

s1.quote: North bommie is covered in glass and cardinal fish that are harassed all day by dozens of coral trout

highlights.text: Bommie with glassfish, coral trout, cleaning station
